newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka remembers victims of human rights abuse.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka remembers victims of human rights abuse.

text.p: Sri Lanka's government, which has been accused of widespread human rights violations, will build a monument to commemorate victims of political violence and rights abuses, a government minister said on Wednesday.

Posts and Telecommunications Minister Mangala Samaraweera said the aim of the Shrine to the Innocents was to remind Sri Lankans of the responsibility they bear for the deaths of countless men, women and children in recent decades.

"In fact we have all been guilty," Samaraweera, who also heads the White Lotus Movement, which was created by the government to promote lasting ethnic harmony in this Indian Ocean island, told reporters.
"The monument will strive to transform the painful memories and the emotionally frozen frustrations of this catastrophic past into a hopeful present and a future of reconciliation."

Thousands of people were killed in two major leftist uprisings in 1971 and the late 1980s and in subsequent crackdowns on suspected leftist insurgents by security forces and pro-government death squads.
Hundreds of government supporters and security personnel also suffered at the hands of the insurgents, who went on the rampage in the late 1980s.
The government says another 50,000 people have been killed in a 13-year-old ethnic war it is still waging against separatist Tamil guerrillas.
The guerrillas, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east, say the death toll is higher.

Sri Lanka has made major strides in restoring its human rights image, Samaraweera said, including establishing a human rights commission and a separate state-run Human Rights Task Force to monitor reported abuses by security forces.

The London-based human rights group Amnesty International in August accused the government of turning a blind eye to widespread violations including extrajudicial executions, disappearances and torture.
The government has denied the charges.
"At least at the moment, human rights abuses are the exception and not the rule," Samaraweera said.
